milestone.title: CI: enforce cargo fmt + clippy --warn in make test and GitHub Actions

intent.outcome: make test fails on fmt violations and clippy warnings, catching regressions before they reach CI. GitHub Actions runs the same gates on every PR.

problem.description: After M-Fmt (cargo fmt) and M-Clippy (warnings resolved), there is no automated gate enforcing either tool. make test and CI only run cargo test. A developer can introduce a clippy warning or forget to run cargo fmt and have it merged without detection.

in_scope: Add 'cargo fmt -- --check' to make test (after existing cargo test call)
Add 'cargo clippy -- -W warnings' to make test (warns but does not deny — WARN-only for the initial adoption; escalate to -D in a follow-up if desired)
Update .github/workflows/plan.yml: add a step that runs 'cargo fmt --check' and 'cargo clippy -- -W warnings' after the existing build steps
Verify make test exits 0 locally after the additions (with the M127+M-Clippy clean baseline)
out_of_scope: Changing clippy to --deny (-D) — that escalation is a separate decision after the warn baseline is proven
Adding new CI jobs beyond what plan.yml already runs
Modifying the existing cargo test step

findings.description: M130 workflow (.github/workflows/plan.yml) lacks an explicit permissions: block. Default token permissions historically grant overly broad scopes (write access to repo contents). M130 is "CI enforcement"; permission scoping is part of CI hygiene. Remediation: add permissions: contents: read at the workflow top level to scope the GITHUB_TOKEN to read-only.
findings.author: external:review-m130

findings.description: M130 workflow pull_request paths filter (lines 7-13) does not cover Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, or Makefile. A PR that adds a dependency (Cargo.toml), updates a transitive (Cargo.lock), or modifies the Makefile will not trigger the validate job, leaving fmt/clippy/validate gates unchecked on that PR. Remediation: extend the paths filter to include Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, and Makefile on both pull_request and push triggers.
findings.author: external:review-m130

findings.description: M130 workflow mp validate step (line 41-45) has continue-on-error: true. This means a non-G8 mp validate error (e.g., a G6 missing-evidence defect, G7 done-without-verified, G8 dependency-not-done on a non-blocked chain) will not fail the CI job. CI is supposed to gate merges; a permissive continue-on-error on a schema/gate validator defeats the purpose of M130. Remediation: remove continue-on-error: true; let the step fail the job on any mp validate error.
findings.author: external:review-m130
